## 1. Study Summary & Metadata Categorization

> **Lung Atlas (Fig 4)** -- Sikkema et al. 2023, *Nature Medicine* 29(6):1563-1577, PMID 37291214. Integrated human lung cell atlas across multiple studies, platforms (`10x`, `BD-Rhapsody`, `Smart-seq2`, `InDrop`), and conditions (`tumor` vs `normal` tissue). Note: The PILOT-GM-VAE paper evaluated `disease` as the biological condition, whereas ECODA also evaluates `origin` (tumor vs normal) and extensive multi-center batch structures.

### Metadata Categories Summary

```{python}
cat_df = ou.categorize_obs_columns(sub.obs, {
    "bio_primary": [BIO_COL, 'disease'],
    "bio_secondary": ECODA_SECONDARY_BIO,
    "batch_candidates": BATCH_COLS,
    "cell_types": ALL_CT_COLS,
    "sample_ids": [SAMPLE_COL, 'donor'],
})
concise_df = ou.summarize_obs_categories(cat_df)
concise_df
```

## 4. Unintegrated Embeddings (Fresh PCA + UMAP)

> **Embedding Protocol:** Computed directly from processed raw counts (total counts normalized to 10k, log1p, 2000 HVGs via Seurat v3 paper flavor, scaled PCA 50 PCs, standard Scanpy UMAP with `min_dist=0.5, spread=1.0`). **No pre-existing or batch-corrected embeddings are used.**

```{python}
label_cols = [c for c in [SAMPLE_COL, BIO_COL] + BATCH_COLS + [CT_COL] if c and c in sub.obs.columns]
um = ou.embed_and_umap_workflow(
    sub, label_cols=label_cols, out_dir=None, name=NAME,
    sample_col=SAMPLE_COL,
)
sub_embedded = um["subset"]

for fig in um["figs"]:
    plt.figure(fig.number)
    plt.show()
```

## 5. Cell-Type Compositional Batch Effect & Statistical Analysis

> **Compositional Protocol:** Evaluates sample-level centered log-ratio (CLR) abundances (+0.5 pseudocount zero-imputation). Group differences are evaluated using two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests (2 groups) or Kruskal-Wallis tests (>2 groups) with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. In addition, multi-variable joint OLS linear regression models ($\text{CLR} \sim \text{cov}_1 + \text{cov}_2 + \dots$) evaluate the joint proportion of variance explained ($R^2$), overall model $F$-statistics, and Type-II ANOVA covariate significance across all clinical and technical variables simultaneously.

```{python}
test_covariates = list(dict.fromkeys([c for c in [BIO_COL, 'disease'] + BATCH_COLS + ECODA_SECONDARY_BIO if c in sub.obs.columns]))

for annot_col in ALL_CT_COLS:
    if annot_col not in sub.obs.columns:
        continue
    clr_curr = ou.compute_clr_composition(sub.obs, SAMPLE_COL, annot_col)
    
    print(f"### Annotation Level: {annot_col} ({clr_curr.shape[1]} Cell Types)")
    
    # 1. Grouped boxplots
    fig_bio = ou.plot_clr_abundance_boxplots(
        clr_curr, sub.obs, SAMPLE_COL, BIO_COL,
        title=f"Compositional CLR Abundance by Biological Condition ({BIO_COL}) — {annot_col}"
    )
    plt.figure(fig_bio.number)
    plt.show()
    
    if BATCH_COLS:
        for bcol in BATCH_COLS[:2]:
            if bcol in sub.obs.columns and sub.obs[bcol].nunique() >= 2:
                fig_batch = ou.plot_clr_abundance_boxplots(
                    clr_curr, sub.obs, SAMPLE_COL, bcol,
                    title=f"Compositional CLR Abundance by Technical Batch ({bcol}) — {annot_col}"
                )
                plt.figure(fig_batch.number)
                plt.show()
                
    # 2. Compositional Significance Heatmap
    sig_mat, fig_sig = ou.compute_compositional_significance_matrix(clr_curr, sub.obs, SAMPLE_COL, test_covariates)
    plt.figure(fig_sig.number)
    plt.show()
    
    # 3. Multi-Variable Joint OLS Linear Model (CLR ~ cov1 + cov2 + ...)
    cov_anova, model_fits, top_summary_txt = ou.compute_compositional_joint_lm(clr_curr, sub.obs, SAMPLE_COL, test_covariates)
    print("Joint Model Covariate Attribution (Type-II ANOVA across all tested variables):")
    display(cov_anova)
    print("Per-Cell-Type Multi-Variable OLS Model Fit Summary:")
    display(model_fits)
```
